lessonRef.title: Publication, presentation, or reflection: predicting and verifying the image of a figure

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: (3, 4) maps to (−3, −4) preserving orientation. Which motion?

steps: Orientation is preserved, so it is a rotation.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Point P(-6, -2) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x + 2, y + 6). Give the image P′.
Reflect the point (3, -1) across the line y = x. Give the image.
Rotate the point (-7, 7) counterclockwise about the origin by 180°. Give the image.
A regular polygon has 3 sides. How many rotations about its centre, strictly between 0° and 360°, carry it onto itself, and what is the smallest such angle?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain your method so that someone who has not done this unit could follow it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has vertices A(5, -8) and B(-8, -5). After a transformation the images are A′(-5, 8) and B′(8, 5), and the triangle keeps its size and orientation sense. Which single rigid motion describes this?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Point P(11, -1) is translated by the rule (x, y) → (x − 5, y − 10). Give the image P′.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
